title: Multiclass feature selection for complementary terahertz discrimination of medicinal materials
abstract: Routine identification of medicinal materials uses established morphological, microscopic and chemical tests. We developed a spectral-selection strategy for complementary terahertz discrimination, using a multiclass ranking front end separated from the final classifier. Absorption and refractive-index exports comprised 1,672 specimens in 18 workbooks. For 300 balanced five-source Suanzaoren specimens, class-specific coefficient stability was aggregated across 20 Monte Carlo draws, with feature budgets and support-vector-machine settings selected within repeated nested validation. Selected absorption achieved 93.44% mean accuracy while retaining an average of 220.6 of 612 coordinates. A full-spectrum SVM on exactly the same partitions achieved 82.67%, a difference of 10.78 percentage points; full-spectrum shrinkage linear discriminant analysis achieved 91.78%. The selected absorption workflow had a descriptive Nogueira stability estimate of 0.8360 across outer refits. Under a separate full-spectrum leave-one-workbook-out protocol, pooled accuracy was 98.84% for Suanzaoren–Zaoren discrimination and 65.61% across all four materials. Additional-label controls in a separate full-spectrum setting increased accuracy from 80.00% to 83.78% with the source scaler and kernel scale frozen. The observed representation, candidate-pool and label-update effects connect discrimination to identifiable analysis choices. The reusable front-end structure and SVM evidence provide a methodological reference for developing further medicinal-material classifiers and extending validation to independent acquisitions.
